narrative: OMX30 opens Tuesday into a mixed technical setup and contradictory macro signals. While the index maintains bull-market structure (+7.3% vs 200-MA, +1.8% vs 50-MA) with strong 90-day momentum (+7.9% ROC), the weak ADX (10.4) undermines conviction, and negative global correlation (-0.348%) warns of contagion risk from DAX (-0.32%) and broad US equity weakness (-0.38% S&P, -0.51% Dow). The spike in US 10Y yields (+46bp to 4.784%) cuts both ways: banks benefit from NIM widening, but tech and high-growth names face DCF compression. Oil's +2.21% surge pressures industrials' input costs. Copper's sharp +3.07% and gold's steady rise provide direct tailwinds for Boliden, but the combination of elevated VIX (+1.63%), weak MACD (below signal), and proximity to 52-week highs (-0.9% from peak) suggests limited upside without clearer risk sentiment reset.
morningBrief: OMX30 expected flat to slightly negative as conflicting signals offset. Global correlation weakness (DAX -32bp, NASDAQ -29bp) and rising yields (US 10Y +46bp) create headwinds despite Swedish bull structure. Watch 3,123–3,130 support (yesterday close ± tight band); resistance 3,155–3,170 (50-MA zone at 3,180 is key gate). Weak ADX (10.4) means reduce position sizing—no trending conviction yet. Sector split: Banks (SEB, Handelsbanken) bid on yield steepness (+NIM), but Industrials (Volvo, Atlas Copco) under pressure from oil costs (+2.21%); Tech (Hexagon, Ericsson) lagging NASDAQ weakness. Boliden the outperformer on copper/gold; watch if commodity strength sustains. US Jobless Claims (14:30 CET) is only major event—soft miss could re-ignite risk rally. Key risk: elevated VIX (15.55) and extended positioning mean sudden reversal if yields cool or tech sentiment flips. Play defensives (Essity, AstraZeneca) if risk-off accelerates.
